import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Lehmer's Mahler measure problem

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lehmer%27s_conjecture)
-/

namespace LehmerMahlerMeasureProblem

open Polynomial LehmerMahlerMeasureProblem

/--
The Mahler measure of `f(X)` is defined as `‖a‖ ∏ᵢ max(1,‖αᵢ‖)`,
where `f(X)=a(X-α₁)(X-α₂)...(X-αₙ)`.
-/
noncomputable def mahlerMeasure (f : ℂ[X]) : ℝ :=
  ‖f.leadingCoeff‖ * (f.roots.map (max 1 ‖·‖)).prod

noncomputable def mahlerMeasureZ (f : ℤ[X]) : ℝ :=
  mahlerMeasure (f.map (algebraMap ℤ ℂ))

/--
Let `M(f)` denote the Mahler measure of `f`.
There exists a constant `μ>1` such that for any `f(x)∈ℤ[x], M(f)>1 → M(f)≥μ`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem lehmer_mahler_measure_problem :
    ∃ μ : ℝ, ∀ f : ℤ[X],
      μ > 1 ∧ (mahlerMeasureZ f > 1 → mahlerMeasureZ f ≥ μ) := by
  sorry

noncomputable def lehmerPolynomial : ℤ[X] := X^10 + X^9 - X^7 - X^6 - X^5 - X^4 - X^3 + X + 1

/--
`μ=M(X^10 + X^9 - X^7 - X^6 - X^5 - X^4 - X^3 + X + 1)` is the best value for `lehmer_mahler_measure_problem`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem lehmer_mahler_measure_problem.variants.best (f : ℤ[X])
    (hf : mahlerMeasureZ f > 1) : mahlerMeasureZ f ≥ mahlerMeasureZ lehmerPolynomial := by
  sorry

/--
If $f$ is not reciprocal and $M(f) > 1$ then $M(f) \ge M(X^3 - X - 1)$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem lehmer_mahler_measure_problem.variants.not_reciprocal (f : ℤ[X])
    (hf : mahlerMeasureZ f > 1) (hf' : f.reverse ≠ f) :
    mahlerMeasureZ f ≥ mahlerMeasureZ (X^3 - X - 1) := by
  sorry

/-- `Polynomial.HasOddCoeffs f` means that all coefficients of `f : Polynomial ℤ` are odd. -/
def Polynomial.HasOddCoeffs (f : Polynomial ℤ) : Prop :=
  ∀ i ≤ f.natDegree, Odd (f.coeff i)

/--
If all the coefficients of $f$ are odd and $M(f) > 1$, then $M(f) \ge M(X^2 - X - 1)$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem lehmer_mahler_measure_problem.variants.odd (f : ℤ[X])
    (hf : mahlerMeasureZ f > 1) (hf' : f.HasOddCoeffs) :
    mahlerMeasureZ f ≥ mahlerMeasureZ (X^2 - X - 1) := by
  sorry

end LehmerMahlerMeasureProblem

findings.description: The theorem omits irreducibility and is false for the reducible polynomials allowed by its hypotheses. Let L = lehmerPolynomial and f = L * X. Then f.reverse ≠ f (their constant coefficients are 1 and 0), but M(f) = M(L) = 1.176280818… > 1, which is less than M(X^3 - X - 1) = 1.324717959…. Lean verified the reverse inequality and preservation of Mahler measure. Merely excluding zero constant coefficients would not suffice: L * (X - 1) also satisfies the displayed hypotheses and has the same measure.
findings.source_evidence: Wikipedia, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lehmer%27s_conjecture, introduces the partial results with “Let P(x) … be an irreducible monic polynomial.” The cited survey, Chris Smyth, “The Mahler measure of algebraic numbers: a survey,” §5.1, https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0701397, states the 1.3247… bound for a nonreciprocal algebraic integer, hence for its irreducible minimal polynomial. Sections 2 and 5.1 give the Mahler measures used in the counterexample.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a hypothesis `(hirr : Irreducible f)` and include this restriction in the docstring. With irreducibility and M(f) > 1, the existing `f.reverse ≠ f` condition suffices. Monicity can also be imposed to follow Wikipedia literally, but is not essential: negation handles leading coefficient -1, and leading-coefficient modulus at least 2 makes the bound automatic.

findings.description: The golden-ratio bound requires nonreciprocity, which is absent from both the theorem and its docstring. The reciprocal polynomial G = X^6 + X^5 - X^4 - X^3 - X^2 + X + 1 has all coefficients odd, yet M(G) = 1.556030191… lies strictly between 1 and M(X^2 - X - 1) = (1 + √5)/2 = 1.618033988…. Thus G satisfies the stated hypotheses and violates the conclusion. Its odd coefficients and reciprocity were verified in Lean; the cited survey explicitly records this polynomial and its measure.
findings.source_evidence: Wikipedia’s “Restricted results” section says “If P(x) is not reciprocal” and then “If further all the coefficients of P are odd,” before giving the golden-ratio bound: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lehmer%27s_conjecture#Restricted_results. Smyth’s survey §5.4, https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0701397, explicitly requires nonreciprocity and gives G with measure 1.556030…. The original Borwein–Hare–Mossinghoff paper’s abstract likewise states the result for “a nonreciprocal polynomial whose coefficients are all odd integers”: https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/S002460930300287X.
findings.suggested_fix: Add nonreciprocity to the hypotheses and docstring. For arbitrary polynomials, follow the survey’s up-to-sign definition (§5.1), using `(hrec : f.reverse ≠ f ∧ f.reverse ≠ -f)`. Adding only `f.reverse ≠ f` would still admit anti-reciprocal polynomials. The odd-coefficient hypothesis already ensures a nonzero constant coefficient.

reformulations.difference: Lean places `μ > 1` inside `∀ f`, whereas the usual statement places it immediately after `∃ μ`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The type ℤ[X] is nonempty. From `∀ f, μ > 1 ∧ Q μ f`, specialize to f = 0 to obtain μ > 1 and take the second component for each f. Conversely, pair a fixed proof of μ > 1 with each proof of Q μ f. The resulting existential statements were proved equivalent in Lean.

reformulations.difference: Lean states a universal lower bound by M(lehmerPolynomial), rather than explicitly asserting that this is the greatest admissible constant.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: M(lehmerPolynomial) > 1, so the polynomial itself attains the proposed minimum. The displayed universal bound makes this constant admissible; applying any other admissible bound to lehmerPolynomial proves it cannot be larger. A Lean proof independently establishes M(lehmerPolynomial) > 1 and proves equivalence with the corresponding `IsGreatest` statement, without using any sorry theorem.

sources_consulted: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lehmer%27s_conjecture — full article, including partial results, restricted results, and status; revision 1358493814.
Chris Smyth, “The Mahler measure of algebraic numbers: a survey,” https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0701397 — v2 LaTeX source, especially §§1, 2, 5.1, and 5.4.

Peter Borwein, Kevin G. Hare, and Michael J. Mossinghoff, “The Mahler measure of polynomials with odd coefficients,” Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society 36 (2004), 332–338, DOI 10.1112/S002460930300287X — publisher abstract at https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/S002460930300287X.
Paul Voutier, “An effective lower bound for the height of algebraic numbers,” https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.3110 — introduction and discussion of Smyth’s bound.
https://mathworld.wolfram.com/LehmersMahlerMeasureProblem.html — statement, proposed minimum, and open status.
Peter Borwein, Edward Dobrowolski, and Michael J. Mossinghoff, “Lehmer’s problem for polynomials with odd coefficients,” https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2007/166-2/p02 — abstract.
review.notes: Checked all four definitions and four theorems. The custom Mahler measure was proved equal to Mathlib’s definition; zero, constants, X, repeated roots, and the odd-coefficient boundary cases were checked. The two open tags agree with the sources; the defects concern hypotheses of solved results, not stale statuses. Successful Lean experiments and a declaration-by-declaration audit are under /workspace/review/. The counterexamples’ numerical Mahler bounds are supported by the cited survey, not claimed as fully formalized numerical inequalities. The target file was not modified.

submission.summary: Added irreducibility to the nonreciprocal variant. Added nonreciprocity up to sign to the odd-coefficient variant, excluding both f.reverse = f and f.reverse = -f. Updated the corresponding docstrings and preserved all other declarations and attributes. The required Lean compile succeeds with only expected `sorry` warnings.
